q: Halogens ($F_2$, $Cl_2$, $Br_2$, $I_2$) are _____ molecules.
e: Halogens (F2, Cl2, Br2, I2) are diatomic molecules. Diatomic is the idea that completes this fact. Monatomic would fill a different blank than diatomic.

q: At room temperature, fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine is a _____, and iodine is a solid.
e: At room temperature, fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine is a liquid, and iodine is a solid. Liquid is the idea that completes this fact. Gas would fill a different blank than liquid.

q: The essential electronic structure of halogens is _____.
e: The essential electronic structure of halogens is ns2 np5. Ns2 np5 is the idea that completes this fact. Ns1 would fill a different blank than ns2 np5.

q: Among the halogens, _____ is the most reactive.
e: Among the halogens, fluorine is the most reactive. Fluorine is the idea that completes this fact. Chlorine would fill a different blank than fluorine.

q: In nature, halogens are found as salts of the _____.
e: In nature, halogens are found as salts of the halides. Halides is the idea that completes this fact. Oxides would fill a different blank than halides.

q: In the laboratory, halogen is prepared by heating sodium or potassium halide with manganese(IV) oxide and _____.
e: In the laboratory, halogen is prepared by heating sodium or potassium halide with manganese(IV) oxide and concentrated sulphuric acid. Concentrated sulphuric acid is the idea that completes this fact. Concentrated nitric acid would fill a different blank than concentrated sulphuric acid.

q: Chlorine is collected by the upward displacement of air because it is slightly soluble in water and _____ than air.
e: Chlorine is collected by the upward displacement of air because it is slightly soluble in water and heavier than air. Heavier is the idea that completes this fact. The same density as would fill a different blank than heavier.

q: Due to its _____ colour, chlorine gas can be seen easily when the gas jar is full.
e: Due to its greenish yellow colour, chlorine gas can be seen easily when the gas jar is full. Greenish yellow is the idea that completes this fact. Pale yellow would fill a different blank than greenish yellow.

q: If required dry, chlorine gas is passed into _____.
e: If required dry, chlorine gas is passed into concentrated sulphuric acid. Concentrated sulphuric acid is the idea that completes this fact. Dilute sulphuric acid would fill a different blank than concentrated sulphuric acid.

q: The chemical equation for the preparation of chlorine is _____.
e: The chemical equation for the preparation of chlorine is 2NaCl(s) + MnO2(s) + 3H2SO4(l) 2NaHSO4(aq) + MnSO4(aq) + Cl2(g) + 2H2O(l). 2NaCl(s) + MnO2(s) + 3H2SO4(l) 2NaHSO4(aq) + MnSO4(aq) + Cl2(g) + 2H2O(l) is the idea that completes this fact. NaCl + H2SO4 to NaHSO4 + HCl would fill a different blank than 2NaCl(s) + MnO2(s) + 3H2SO4(l) 2NaHSO4(aq) + MnSO4(aq) + Cl2(g) + 2H2O(l).

q: Fluorine is a very _____ gas.
e: Fluorine is a very pale yellow gas. Pale yellow is the idea that completes this fact. Reddish brown would fill a different blank than pale yellow.

q: Fluorine reacts with almost all other elements, except _____.
e: Fluorine reacts with almost all other elements, except helium and neon. Helium and neon is the idea that completes this fact. Oxygen and nitrogen would fill a different blank than helium and neon.

q: Chlorine is a _____ gas with a choking, unpleasant smell.
e: Chlorine is a pale green gas with a choking, unpleasant smell. Pale green is the idea that completes this fact. Purple-black would fill a different blank than pale green.

q: Chlorine is about _____ times as dense as air.
e: Chlorine is about 2.5 times as dense as air. 2.5 is the idea that completes this fact. 1.5 would fill a different blank than 2.5.

q: Bromine is a heavy, reddish brown, _____ liquid.
e: Bromine is a heavy, reddish brown, volatile liquid. Volatile is the idea that completes this fact. Non-volatile would fill a different blank than volatile.

q: Bromine is slightly soluble in water, forming a _____ solution containing about 3 percent of bromine at ordinary temperature.
e: Bromine is slightly soluble in water, forming a yellowish red solution containing about 3 percent of bromine at ordinary temperature. Yellowish red is the idea that completes this fact. Violet would fill a different blank than yellowish red.

q: Iodine is a _____ shiny solid with an irritating smell.
e: Iodine is a purple-black shiny solid with an irritating smell. Purple-black is the idea that completes this fact. Pale green would fill a different blank than purple-black.

q: Iodine sublimes rapidly when heated, forming a _____ vapour.
e: Iodine sublimes rapidly when heated, forming a violet vapour. Violet is the idea that completes this fact. Yellow would fill a different blank than violet.

q: Iodine is almost insoluble in water but readily dissolves in aqueous potassium iodide to form a _____ solution.
e: Iodine is almost insoluble in water but readily dissolves in aqueous potassium iodide to form a brown solution. Brown is the idea that completes this fact. Violet would fill a different blank than brown.

q: Iodine dissolves in carbon disulphide and carbon tetrachloride, forming _____ solutions.
e: Iodine dissolves in carbon disulphide and carbon tetrachloride, forming violet solutions. Violet is the idea that completes this fact. Green would fill a different blank than violet.

q: The reactivity of halogens occurs in the order of _____.
e: The reactivity of halogens occurs in the order of F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2. F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2 is the idea that completes this fact. Cl2 > F2 > Br2 > I2 would fill a different blank than F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2.

q: When a tube containing equal volumes of chlorine and hydrogen is exposed to sunlight, it _____.
e: When a tube containing equal volumes of chlorine and hydrogen is exposed to sunlight, it explodes. Explodes is the idea that completes this fact. Slowly reacts would fill a different blank than explodes.

q: Chlorine reacts vigorously with metals to form _____.
e: Chlorine reacts vigorously with metals to form metal chlorides. Metal chlorides is the idea that completes this fact. Metal hydrides would fill a different blank than metal chlorides.

q: When a very thin sheet of an alloy of copper and zinc is dropped into a chlorine gas jar, it burns brightly with a _____ flame.
e: When a very thin sheet of an alloy of copper and zinc is dropped into a chlorine gas jar, it burns brightly with a green flame. Green is the idea that completes this fact. Yellow would fill a different blank than green.

q: Phosphorus burns spontaneously in chlorine to form phosphorus(III) chloride and _____.
e: Phosphorus burns spontaneously in chlorine to form phosphorus(III) chloride and phosphorus(V) chloride. Phosphorus(V) chloride is the idea that completes this fact. Phosphorus hydride would fill a different blank than phosphorus(V) chloride.

q: Among halogens, chlorine and bromine have bleaching power, however, _____ does not.
e: Among halogens, chlorine and bromine have bleaching power, however, iodine does not. Iodine is the idea that completes this fact. Fluorine is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Chlorine reacts with water to form HOCl and _____.
e: Chlorine reacts with water to form HOCl and HCl. HCl is the idea that completes this fact. O2 would fill a different blank than HCl.

q: The HOCl slowly decomposes to hydrochloric acid and _____.
e: The HOCl slowly decomposes to hydrochloric acid and nascent oxygen. Oxygen supports respiration and combustion, and it is a very reactive non-metal. Chlorine gas would fill a different blank than nascent oxygen.

q: The nascent oxygen bleaches dyes by _____ them.
e: The nascent oxygen bleaches dyes by oxidising them. Oxidising is the idea that completes this fact. Reducing would fill a different blank than oxidising.

q: Chlorine will bleach moist litmus papers. This is used as a test for _____.
e: Chlorine will bleach moist litmus papers. This is used as a test for chlorine. Chlorine is the idea that completes this fact. Oxygen would fill a different blank than chlorine.

q: Halogens are _____ agents.
e: Halogens are oxidising agents. Oxidising is the idea that completes this fact. Reducing would fill a different blank than oxidising.

q: Chlorine oxidises iron(II) chloride into _____.
e: Chlorine oxidises iron(II) chloride into iron(III) chloride. Iron(III) chloride is the idea that completes this fact. Iron metal would fill a different blank than iron(III) chloride.

q: Iodine oxidises hydrogen sulphide to form hydrogen iodide and liberate _____.
e: Iodine oxidises hydrogen sulphide to form hydrogen iodide and liberate sulphur. Sulphur is the idea that completes this fact. Oxygen would fill a different blank than sulphur.

q: Chlorine reacts with cold dilute potassium hydroxide to form potassium chloride, potassium hypochlorite and _____.
e: Chlorine reacts with cold dilute potassium hydroxide to form potassium chloride, potassium hypochlorite and water. Water is the idea that completes this fact. Hydrogen would fill a different blank than water.

q: Chlorine reacts with hot concentrated potassium hydroxide to form potassium chloride, potassium chlorate and _____.
e: Chlorine reacts with hot concentrated potassium hydroxide to form potassium chloride, potassium chlorate and water. Water is the idea that completes this fact. Hydrogen would fill a different blank than water.

q: When chlorine is passed into a solution of sodium bromide, the respective halogen is displaced by more reactive chlorine to form sodium chloride and _____.
e: When chlorine is passed into a solution of sodium bromide, the respective halogen is displaced by more reactive chlorine to form sodium chloride and bromine. Bromine is the idea that completes this fact. Fluorine would fill a different blank than bromine.

q: When bromine is passed into a solution of sodium iodide, _____ is liberated.
e: When bromine is passed into a solution of sodium iodide, iodine is liberated. Iodine is the idea that completes this fact. Chlorine would fill a different blank than iodine.

q: Iodine cannot displace chlorine and bromine from their salt solutions because it is _____ reactive.
e: Iodine cannot displace chlorine and bromine from their salt solutions because it is less reactive. Less is the idea that completes this fact. More would fill a different blank than less.

q: A halide ion is a halogen atom with a _____ charge.
e: A halide ion is a halogen atom with a negative charge. Negative is the idea that completes this fact. Neutral would fill a different blank than negative.

q: The presence of chloride, bromide or iodide ions can be tested by adding _____ solution.
e: The presence of chloride, bromide or iodide ions can be tested by adding silver nitrate solution. Acidified silver nitrate is a test for chloride: a white precipitate of AgCl appears. Sodium hydroxide would fill a different blank than silver nitrate.

q: Samples for the silver nitrate test are typically acidified with dilute nitric acid to remove interfering ions, e.g., _____ ions.
e: Samples for the silver nitrate test are typically acidified with dilute nitric acid to remove interfering ions, e.g., carbonate ions. Carbonate is the idea that completes this fact. Nitrate would fill a different blank than carbonate.

q: In the silver nitrate test for halides, different colours of _____ precipitates are observed.
e: In the silver nitrate test for halides, different colours of silver halide precipitates are observed. Silver halide is the idea that completes this fact. Silver oxide would fill a different blank than silver halide.

q: Fluorine is used in the form of fluorides in drinking water to prevent tooth decay by hardening the _____ on teeth.
e: Fluorine is used in the form of fluorides in drinking water to prevent tooth decay by hardening the enamel on teeth. Enamel is the idea that completes this fact. Dentine would fill a different blank than enamel.

q: Chlorine is used to make PVC (Polyvinyl chloride) plastic as well as household _____.
e: Chlorine is used to make PVC (Polyvinyl chloride) plastic as well as household bleaches. Bleaches is the idea that completes this fact. Fuels would fill a different blank than bleaches.

q: Bromine is used to make disinfectants, medicines and _____.
e: Bromine is used to make disinfectants, medicines and fire retardants. Fire retardants is the idea that completes this fact. Glass would fill a different blank than fire retardants.

q: Iodine is used in medicines to treat cases of _____ and as a disinfectant (e.g., 'Tincture of iodine').
e: Iodine is used in medicines to treat cases of goiter and as a disinfectant (e.g., 'Tincture of iodine'). Goiter is the idea that completes this fact. Scurvy would fill a different blank than goiter.

q: Halides are widely used in metal halide lamps that are _____.
e: Halides are widely used in metal halide lamps that are high-intensity discharge lamps. High-intensity discharge lamps is the idea that completes this fact. Low-intensity discharge lamps would fill a different blank than high-intensity discharge lamps.
